description: The cheapest time a page can save is time it spends before any of its own code runs. Redirects, uncompressed text, cold origins and re-fetched static assets are all paid before the first byte of content arrives, and none of them are visible in the source of the page they slow down.

gates.title: The Canonical Host Answers Directly
gates.rule: The host people actually reach - with and without www - serves the document itself rather than redirecting to the other one. A redirect is a whole round trip on a cold mobile connection before the browser has learned there is a page.
gates.fix: Serve both hosts from the same deployment, or make the redirect one hop to the canonical host and point every link, sitemap entry and canonical tag at that host.

gates.title: Text Assets Are Compressed
gates.rule: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON and SVG arrive brotli or gzip encoded. Uncompressed JavaScript is roughly four times the bytes for the same behaviour, and the difference is paid on every cold visit.
gates.fix: Enable brotli at the edge. On a platform that does it by default, confirm it rather than assuming it.

gates.title: Hashed Assets Are Cached Forever
gates.rule: Every asset whose filename carries a content hash is served immutable with a year-long max-age. A hashed file cannot go stale by definition, so revalidating it spends a request to be told nothing changed.
gates.fix: Set Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable on the hashed asset directory.

gates.title: The Document Declares Its Own Freshness
gates.rule: The HTML carries an explicit cache policy. Left unset, a CDN invents one, and the two failure modes are a document cached past a deploy and a document never cached at all.
gates.fix: Set an explicit Cache-Control on the document, with stale-while-revalidate where the platform honours it.

gates.title: Origins On The Critical Path Are Preconnected
gates.rule: Every origin the first screen depends on is preconnected. A cold origin costs DNS, TCP and TLS before the first byte of whatever it was fetching, and the browser cannot start any of that until it finds the reference.
gates.fix: Add rel=preconnect for the origins the first screen needs and rel=dns-prefetch for the rest. Preconnect costs a connection, so it is for the few that matter.

gates.title: No Third-Party Script Blocks The Document
gates.rule: Analytics, tag managers, chat widgets and pixels carry defer or async, or are loaded after paint. A third party in the critical path hands a stranger control of when the page appears.
gates.fix: Add defer or async. Load anything that is not needed for the first screen after the load event.

gates.title: The Document Arrives Quickly
gates.rule: Time to first byte stays under 800ms at the 75th percentile. Everything else in this checklist starts counting from the moment the document lands, so a slow origin moves every metric at once.
gates.fix: Serve the document from the edge, cache it, and take the database out of the request path that renders it.

gates.title: Nothing Is Fetched That Is Never Used
gates.rule: The first screen requests no asset it does not render - no preload for a font weight nothing sets, no image for a carousel slide two, no stylesheet for a route nobody is on. A preload for an unused asset is strictly worse than no preload, because it competes with the ones that matter.
gates.fix: Remove the preload, or use the asset it names on the first screen.
